pr_title: Bluetooth: Controller: Implement Periodic Advertiser List
pr_body:
Implement support for Periodic Advertiser List to be used
in LE Periodic Advertising Create Sync command.

Fixes #38316.

Signed-off-by: Vinayak Kariappa Chettimada <vich@nordicsemi.no>
pr_comments: @carlescufi Request your attention to this commit  https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/38338/commits/4bc5d45b388c762b786dc8b999eea4e0e06f8079 in this PR which partly handles inclusive naming related to filter implementation in the Controller. Your review is welcome here in this PR until the commit is ready to be cherry-picked out of this PR (so that other commits in this PR will have reduced rework effort)

@cvinayak I feel like this PR is becoming a catch-all for several issue (updates to filter accept list and addition of `const`), and that kind of distracts from what the PR should be doing. 

Since I've already reviewed it, it's okay for me to keep as is, but probably beneficial for others if those changes were split to 3 PRs.

issue_context.title: Synchronize multiple DF TX devices in the DF Connectionless RX Example "Periodic Advertising list"
issue_context.body:
I got an Unknown Command error while working with the periodic advertising list feature #29127

When I tried to add the device to the Periodic Advertising list or clear the Periodic Advertising list, **error -5** shows over the terminal after deep looking at the source code found the reason for such error is that commands (BT_HCI_OP_LE_ADD_DEV_TO_PER_ADV_LIST, BT_HCI_OP_LE_REM_DEV_FROM_PER_ADV_LIST, BT_HCI_OP_LE_CLEAR_PER_ADV_LIST, BT_HCI_OP_LE_READ_PER_ADV_LIST_SIZE) are not defined/handled in the **static int controller_cmd_handle(uint16_t  ocf, struct net_buf *cmd, struct net_buf **evt, void **node_rx)** function.

Is there any way to solve such a bug, kindly guide me?
comments: Periodic Advertising List in the Controller is work in progress, please try this PR: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/38338

@Thalley Does the host support synchronization from periodic advertising lists?

Shouldn't this check addresses in the list? https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/f50574a6a0773e74efb468265ac94cdbabeb97c1/subsys/bluetooth/host/scan.c#L696-L702

> @Thalley Does the host support synchronization from periodic advertising lists?
> 
> Shouldn't this check addresses in the list?
> 
> https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/f50574a6a0773e74efb468265ac94cdbabeb97c1/subsys/bluetooth/host/scan.c#L696-L702

Yes, that is actually still missing. Basically we need to implement this paragraph: 
> If the Periodic Advertiser List is not used, the Advertising_SID, Advertiser Address_Type, and Advertiser Address parameters specify the periodic advertising device to listen to; otherwise they shall be ignored.

So if the option to use the list is set, then we shall ignore the address parameters and instead either just accept it, or store the list in the host and validate whether the address of the event is in the list. The former is the simpler solution, and I am not sure if we need to validate the address in the host.

review_comments:
```suggestion
static void le_rem_dev_from_per_adv_list(struct net_buf *buf, struct net_buf **evt)
```
I am against use of `PER` as it is abbreviation for Peripheral in the Bluetooth Test Specification.

So if not `pal` and not `per_adv_list`, I guess we are just left with `pa_list` or `periodic_adv_list` (or even `periodic_advertiser_list`). 

We use `per_` for periodic in the Host API though.

Naming is outside the scope of this PR, now that the names have been changed thrice in this PR. 

That said, `per_` as abbreviation in BT API is sad as `per` is a word in itself having different meaning.

I suggest a issue be open to discuss general changes to abbreviations used in the Bluetooth Subsystem, and no change be done without a consensus.
@cvinayak then please open the issue and after that I'll resolve my comments about naming.
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/39025
Thank you!

```suggestion
static void le_clear_per_adv_list(struct net_buf *buf, struct net_buf **evt)
```
Wouldn't it be better to create a function for that. It would make debugging experience better. From efficiency point of view if should not change anything.
The macro is following a similar `LIST_MATCH` macro used in the filter accept list implementation.
Ok, then let it stay. But for future is seems to me that it would be more beneficial to use functions instead of macros like this one.
Agree, I will make the change as part of the extended advertising filtering implementation changes I am working on currently.
Can the same address be stored in `fal` and `pal`?
yes.

Out of curiosity, I didn't spot earlier that `uint8_t parameters were declared as `const` in controller code.
It is something that we should start to consider as policy?

At least the `const uint8_t *` should be used IMO, as that gives useful information to the caller. 

The `* const` has less of an impact IMO, but it does prevent someone from accidentally overwriting the pointer in the function, which does make sense. 

The only argument I have for not using `const uint8_t *const` is that it looks ugly :D
I have no objections about both (and yes it look ugly ;-)). I just wanted to get consensus whether we start to consider it as recommendation or enforce it.

This is the prototype for `memcpy`, it isnt ugly to me, but it is something it is.

`void *memcpy(void *restrict dest, const void *restrict src, size_t n);`
Concluding, should I consider usage of const pointers wherever possible as recommendation in controller's code or enforce it in my code and in reviews?
Internal coding style enforces strict usage of variable qualifiers, but I am open to what is acceptable in the Zephyr code base.
Then let we know everything. Qualifiers will be enforced.

```suggestion
static void le_add_dev_to_per_adv_list(struct net_buf *buf, struct net_buf **evt)
```
The `pal` abbreviation was suggested by me, mainly because the abbreviate makes sense, but also since we updated the whitelist (now called filter accept list) to `fal`.

Thanks for bringing more context to the topic. In my humble opinion it is a bit confusing. This is another abbreviation that is ok for people with experience in controller programming (are familiar with language/abbreviations used there). It may be intimidating for new people to start contributing to controller because it makes the code reading harder. The learning curve, that is already pretty steep, gets even steeper.

@Thalley my feelings about `FAL` are the same as for `PAL`. Is there a `FAL` acronym mentioned in the BT Core spec?

BTW. If there were a PAL used for something else, even though is was removed in 5.3, people may be confused.
From what I can tell, neither FAL or PAL is used in the spec, and both are always written fully.

> 
> 
> Thanks for bringing more context to the topic. In my humble opinion it is a bit confusing. This is another abbreviation that is ok for people with experience in controller programming (are familiar with language/abbreviations used there). It may be intimidating for new people to start contributing to controller because it makes the code reading harder. The learning curve, that is already pretty steep, gets even steeper.

As a person with the least knowledge around Zephyr (compared to others at this discussion), I agree with @ppryga . It becomes hard to understand, Also I can see in other files, similar approach is not used, especially when "app developers" will use the header file (and is not mainly developed for kernel uses).

I agree, `FAL` and `PAL` are as bad compare to `GATT` or `EATT` or `L2CAP` or `L2CAP ECFC`. Yes, PAL and FAL do not have entries in the Bluetooth Specification's abbreviation table; sources have comments with expansions for FAL and PAL.
The same comment applies here: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/38338#discussion_r719292963

Similar thing like for `PAL_ADDR_MATCH`, maybe a function instead?
Resolving with the same justification as `PAL_ADDR_MATCH`.
This adds another 40 lines to a function that's almost 500 lines long. I strongly suggest that we look into splitting this function.
I will refactor in a separate commit in this PR
